title: Edge telemetry regulator: deterministic fingerprint sessionization for structured log ingress
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: High-velocity edge clients send semi-structured logs without reliable correlation IDs. This causes noisy joins in Loki and elastic backends, high downstream fanout, miss-attribution of latency/errors, and costly re-ingestion.

Goal: Implement a lightweight 'edge telemetry regulator' (ETR) sidecar/proxy that deterministically fingerprints session affinity, synthesizes stable correlation IDs when missing, performs best-effort KV enrichment from a local cache, and routes or annotates events with tenant-aware shard headers to reduce downstream fanout. The ETR should be small (Rust/gRPC or lightweight Go) and add minimal CPU/latency at the edge (target <2ms p50 extra).

Key features: deterministic fingerprinting using ordered attribute set (user_agent, ip_hash, cookie_token, request_path) -> SHA256 truncated to 64bits, fallback priority list, TTL-based session glueing; synth corr_id when absent and mark as synthesized; inline KV enrichment (service name, runtime, instance_id) using LRU cache with async background refresh; per-tenant priority tags for canary vs normal traffic; routing header (x-rw-shard) to influence Loki/ELK partitioning; backpressure response codes and sampling hints for upstream when ingestion pressure is high.

Compatibility: Works for structured JSON and JSONL, exports Loki-compatible labels and an optional elastic-compatible _meta block. Should integrate with existing ingest gateway or run as sidecar for dedicated private deployments.

Success metrics: reduce downstream fanout by 35% for multi-tenant ingestion paths; increase corr_id coverage to >98% for edge traffic; reduce late-join reingest incidents by 90% in first month after rollout.
updates: 2026-02-10: Spec drafted (this ticket). Core design decision: deterministic fingerprint over random UUID for reproducible session grouping across retries.

2026-02-16: PoC implemented (Go) demonstrating fingerprint generation and synthesized corr_id; local LRU cache stub added for KV enrichment. p50 latency added: 1.6ms, p95: 3.8ms on t3.medium equivalent.

2026-02-20: Benchmarked shard header routing against current fanout. Synthetic load test shows 40% reduction in cross-tenant fanout for multi-service traces when x-rw-shard respected by downstream. Added feature flag gate for synthesized IDs. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/PR-412

2026-02-24: Integration test with Loki staging pipeline passed (labels preserved, queries work with fingerprint label). Identified need for a deterministic sort order when building fingerprint to avoid attribute set variability. Added attribute canonicalizer.
2026-03-01: Security review prep started. Draft runbook for rollback and monitoring created. Preparing design doc for Console team to expose per-tenant canary toggles.
comments: Elena Korhonen (Design): Please ensure synthesized corr_id is visually distinguishable in Console and API so customers know it's generated. Suggest suffix '-synth' in corr_id string.
Michael Chen (SRE): Concern on CPU at high QPS. Recommend adding a compiled path that uses a simple XXHash for fingerprinting if attribute set small; fallback to SHA256 when entropy low.
Priya Nair (PM): Tie rollout to cost dashboard and create alert for anything >10% increase in ingest CPU or >5% tail latency regression. Add a label to track canary tenants.
notes: Implementation must preserve original event fields and only add synthetic corr_id when missing. All synthesized IDs must be deterministic per session window and include a flag in metadata so downstream systems can optionally ignore them for security/audit-sensitive tenants. Will add feature-flag to disable synthesis per tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Edge proxy can attach corr_id for >98% of events missing corrid without altering original payload semantics.
Queries that use the fingerprint label in Loki return consistent session slices across retries and producer restarts.
No more than 10% increase in p95 ingest latency for a single node at target QPS during canary.
Canary deployment workflow exists (tenant toggle in Console) and rollback runbook validated.
